questions.prompt: Write 21:30 as a 12-hour time. Use am or pm.
questions.explanation: 21 is more than 12, so it is pm. 21 − 12 = 9. So 9:30 pm.

questions.prompt: Write 13:05 as a 12-hour time. Use am or pm.
questions.explanation: 13 − 12 = 1, and it is after noon. So 1:05 pm.

questions.prompt: Which of these 24-hour times is in the afternoon?
questions.explanation: Afternoon times are after 12:00. Only 14:20 is after 12:00. It is 2:20 pm.

questions.prompt: It is evening. Write the time on the clock as a 24-hour time.
questions.explanation: The clock shows 10:50. It is evening, so add 12: 10 + 12 = 22. So 22:50.

questions.prompt: Put these times in order, from earliest to latest in the day.
questions.explanation: 24-hour times can be ordered by the hour first: 07, 10, 12, 16, 21.

questions.prompt:
Gabriel says 19:00 is 9 pm.
The correct 12-hour time is ___ pm.
questions.explanation: Take away 12, not 10: 19 − 12 = 7. So 19:00 is 7 pm.
questions.misconception: Takes away 10 from the hour instead of 12.

questions.prompt: Ellie says 4:15 pm is later in the day than 16:40. Is she right?
questions.explanation: Change 16:40 to a 12-hour time: 16 − 12 = 4, so it is 4:40 pm. 4:40 pm is later than 4:15 pm.
options: No, they are the same time

questions.prompt: A train leaves at 23:20. The trip takes 50 minutes. What time does the train arrive? Write it as a 24-hour time.
questions.explanation: 23:20 to 00:00 (midnight) is 40 minutes. 10 more minutes takes it to 00:10.

units.title: Seconds, days, months and years
units.summary: There are 60 seconds in a minute and 60 minutes in an hour. A year has 365 days, or 366 in a leap year, when February has 29 days.

questions.prompt: How many seconds are there in 3 minutes?
questions.explanation: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 + 60 + 60 = 180 seconds.

questions.prompt: How many days are there in September?
questions.explanation: September has 30 days, like April, June and November.

questions.prompt: Which of these months have 31 days? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: January, July and December have 31 days. April and November have 30.

questions.prompt: How many hours are there in 2 days?
questions.explanation: 1 day = 24 hours. 24 + 24 = 48 hours.

questions.prompt: Put these in order, from shortest to longest.
questions.explanation: Change them to seconds: 45, 60, 100 and 120 seconds.

questions.prompt: How many days are there in June and July together?
questions.explanation: June has 30 days and July has 31. 30 + 31 = 61.

questions.prompt: Which is longer, 150 seconds or 2 minutes?
questions.explanation: 2 minutes = 120 seconds. 150 seconds is longer.

questions.prompt:
Ezra says there are 100 seconds in a minute, so 2 minutes is 200 seconds.
2 minutes is really ___ seconds.
questions.explanation: 1 minute = 60 seconds, not 100. 60 + 60 = 120 seconds.
questions.misconception: Thinks time units go in 100s like cm and m.

questions.prompt: True or false?
questions.explanation: October has 31 days. A week has 7 days, so 2 weeks = 14 days.

statements.s: February has 29 days in a leap year.
There are 12 months in a year.

questions.prompt: 2028 is a leap year. How many days are there in January and February 2028 altogether?
questions.explanation: January has 31 days. In a leap year February has 29 days. 31 + 29 = 60.

units.title: How long does it take?
units.summary: To find how long something takes, count on from the start time to the end time. Jump to the next o'clock first, then add on the rest of the minutes.

questions.prompt: A lesson starts at 9:00 and ends at 9:45. How long is the lesson?
questions.explanation: From 9:00 to 9:45 is 45 minutes.

questions.prompt: A puppet show starts at 2:15 and ends at 2:40. How long does it last?
questions.explanation: Count on from 15 minutes past to 40 minutes past: 40 − 15 = 25 minutes.

questions.prompt: Swimming starts at 4:50 and ends at 5:30. How long is it?
questions.explanation: 4:50 to 5:00 is 10 minutes. 5:00 to 5:30 is 30 minutes. 10 + 30 = 40.

questions.prompt: Tia's walk to school takes 22 minutes. Ollie's walk takes 35 minutes. How much longer is Ollie's walk?
questions.explanation: 35 − 22 = 13 minutes.

questions.prompt: A pie goes into the oven at 5:40. It needs 35 minutes. What time should it come out?
questions.explanation: 5:40 + 20 minutes = 6:00. 15 more minutes takes it to 6:15.

questions.prompt: True or false?
questions.explanation: 3:10 to 3:50 is 40 minutes. 7:45 to 8:00 is 15 minutes and 8:00 to 8:20 is 20, so 35. 11:30 to 12:00 is 30 and 12:00 to 12:05 is 5, so 35, not 45.

questions.prompt: A bike ride starts at 10:20 and ends at 11:55. How long is it in minutes?
questions.explanation: 10:20 to 11:20 is 1 hour = 60 minutes. 11:20 to 11:55 is 35 minutes. 60 + 35 = 95 minutes.

questions.prompt:
Ada says 6:45 to 7:15 is 70 minutes because 715 − 645 = 70.
It is really ___ minutes.
questions.explanation: There are 60 minutes in an hour, not 100. 6:45 to 7:00 is 15 minutes. 7:00 to 7:15 is 15 minutes. 15 + 15 = 30.
questions.misconception: Subtracts times as if there were 100 minutes in an hour.

questions.prompt: A film lasts 1 hour 20 minutes. It ends at 4:10 pm. What time did it start?
questions.explanation: Count back 1 hour from 4:10 pm: 3:10 pm. Count back 20 minutes more: 2:50 pm.

questions.prompt: 3 races each last 15 minutes. There is a 5 minute break after the 1st race and after the 2nd race. The 1st race starts at 1:40 pm. What time does the last race end?
questions.explanation: Races: 15 × 3 = 45 minutes. Breaks: 5 + 5 = 10 minutes. Total 55 minutes. 1:40 pm + 20 minutes = 2:00 pm, then 35 more minutes = 2:35 pm.

units.title: Drawing 2-D shapes
units.summary: A polygon is a flat shape with straight sides, named by counting them: 5 sides make a pentagon and 6 sides make a hexagon. Use a ruler to draw the sides.

questions.prompt: Name this shape.
questions.explanation: Count the straight sides: there are 5. A 5-sided shape is a pentagon.

questions.prompt: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.explanation: A hexagon has 6 straight sides.

questions.prompt: Match the number of sides to the shape name.
questions.explanation: Tri means 3, quad means 4, hex means 6 and oct means 8.

questions.prompt: How many vertices (corners) does an octagon have?
questions.explanation: A polygon has the same number of vertices as sides. An octagon has 8 sides, so 8 vertices.

questions.prompt: Which of these are quadrilaterals? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral is any shape with 4 straight sides. Squares, rectangles and kites all have 4.

questions.prompt: Jin joins dots on a grid with straight lines to make a closed shape with 5 sides. What shape has Jin drawn?
questions.explanation: Any closed shape with 5 straight sides is a pentagon, even if the sides are different lengths.

questions.prompt: How many sides do 2 triangles and 1 hexagon have altogether?
questions.explanation: 2 triangles: 3 + 3 = 6 sides. A hexagon has 6. 6 + 6 = 12.

questions.prompt: Rosa says a circle is a polygon because it is a flat shape. Is she right?
questions.explanation: A polygon must be flat and have only straight sides. A circle is flat, but its edge is curved.
questions.misconception: Thinks every flat shape is a polygon.
options: Yes, all flat shapes are polygons
No, a polygon has straight sides and a circle has a curved edge
No, because a circle is a 3-D shape

questions.prompt: True or false?
questions.explanation: Triangles have 3 straight sides. Pentagons can have sides of different lengths, so they do not all look the same. 8 − 6 = 2.

statements.s: A triangle can have a curved side.
An octagon has 2 more sides than a hexagon.
All pentagons look exactly the same.

questions.prompt: Explain how to draw a rectangle 4 cm long and 2 cm wide on 1 cm squared paper.
questions.explanation: A rectangle has 2 pairs of equal sides and 4 right angles. On 1 cm squared paper, each square is 1 cm, so count 4 squares and 2 squares.
questions.model: Use a ruler and draw a line 4 squares long. From each end, draw a line 2 squares long at a right angle, following the grid lines. Join the 2 ends with a line 4 squares long.
checklist: Uses a ruler for straight lines
Draws 2 sides of 4 cm and 2 sides of 2 cm
Makes the corners right angles, for example by following the grid lines

units.title: 3-D shapes
units.summary: 3-D shapes have faces, edges and vertices. A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices, and it is still a cube whichever way up it is.

questions.prompt: Which 3-D shape is a football like?
questions.explanation: A football is round all over, like a sphere.

questions.prompt: A dice is a cube. How many faces does it have?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 square faces: top, bottom, front, back and 2 sides.

questions.prompt: Match each object to its shape.
questions.explanation: A tin has 2 circle faces and a curved side. A dice has 6 square faces. A cereal box has 6 rectangle faces.

questions.prompt: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
questions.explanation: Each triangle end has 3 edges: 3 + 3 = 6. 3 more edges join the ends. 6 + 3 = 9.

questions.prompt: How many vertices does a square-based pyramid have?
questions.explanation: The square base has 4 vertices, and there is 1 at the top. 4 + 1 = 5.

questions.prompt: I have 2 flat circular faces and 1 curved surface. What shape am I?
questions.explanation: A cylinder has a circle at each end joined by a curved surface.

questions.prompt: Rhian makes a triangular prism from straws and balls of modelling clay. Each vertex is a ball of clay. How many balls of clay does she need?
questions.explanation: Each triangle end has 3 vertices. 3 + 3 = 6 balls of clay.

questions.prompt: Nia says a cone has 2 faces: a circle and a triangle. Is she right?
questions.explanation: A cone looks like a triangle from the side, but that side is a curved surface, not a flat triangle face.
questions.misconception: Thinks the side view of a cone is a flat triangle face.
options: Yes, a cone has a circle face and a triangle face
No, a cone has 1 flat circle face and 1 curved surface
No, a cone has no faces at all

questions.prompt: True or false?
questions.explanation: A cylinder has no vertices because it has no corners. A triangular prism has 2 triangle faces and 3 rectangle faces: 5 in all.

questions.prompt: I have 5 faces. 2 of my faces are triangles and 3 are rectangles. What shape am I?
questions.explanation: 2 triangle ends joined by 3 rectangles make a triangular prism.

units.title: Angles and turns
units.summary: An angle is an amount of turn, and a quarter turn is 1 right angle. Half a turn is 2 right angles, and a complete turn is 4.

questions.prompt: How many right angles make a half turn?
questions.explanation: A quarter turn is 1 right angle. 2 quarter turns make a half turn, so 2 right angles.

questions.prompt: A complete turn is how many right angles?
questions.explanation: 4 quarter turns bring you all the way round, so 4 right angles.

questions.prompt: The minute hand of a clock points to 12. It makes a quarter turn clockwise. Where does it point now?
questions.explanation: A quarter of the way round the clock from 12 is 3.

questions.prompt: Match each turn to the number of right angles.
questions.explanation: Each quarter turn is 1 right angle, so count the quarters.

questions.prompt: The minute hand moves clockwise from 6 to 9. What turn is that?
questions.explanation: 6 to 9 is a quarter of the way round the clock, so it is a quarter turn.

questions.prompt: How many angles are there inside a hexagon?
questions.explanation: A polygon has the same number of angles inside it as sides. A hexagon has 6 sides, so 6 angles.

questions.prompt: The minute hand moves clockwise from 2 to 8. What turn is that?
questions.explanation: 2 to 8 is halfway round the clock, so it is a half turn: 2 right angles.

questions.prompt:
Leo says turning clockwise from 12 to 9 is a quarter turn.
It is really a ___ turn, which is ___ right angles.
questions.explanation: Going clockwise from 12 you pass 3, then 6, then reach 9. That is 3 quarter turns. Leo turned the other way in his head.
questions.misconception: Ignores the direction of the turn.

questions.prompt: True or false?
questions.explanation: A half turn is 2 right angles. A three-quarter turn one way lands where a quarter turn the other way does.

statements.s: 2 quarter turns make a half turn.
A three-quarter turn clockwise ends facing the same way as a quarter turn anticlockwise.
A half turn is 3 right angles.
A square has 4 angles inside it.

questions.prompt:
Face the door. Make a half turn clockwise, then a quarter turn anticlockwise.
You would end up in the same place with just a ___ turn clockwise.
questions.explanation: A half turn clockwise is 2 right angles. Turning back 1 right angle leaves 2 − 1 = 1 right angle clockwise, which is a quarter turn.

units.title: Right angles
units.summary: A right angle is a quarter turn, like the corner of a book. Compare other angles with a right angle to say whether they are smaller or greater.

questions.prompt: Is this angle less than, equal to or greater than a right angle?
questions.explanation: The 2 lines make a square corner, so it is a right angle.

questions.prompt: Is this angle less than, equal to or greater than a right angle?
questions.explanation: The opening is narrower than a square corner, so it is less than a right angle.

questions.prompt: Is this angle less than, equal to or greater than a right angle?
questions.explanation: The opening is wider than a square corner, so it is greater than a right angle.

questions.prompt: How many right angles are there inside a rectangle?
questions.explanation: All 4 corners of a rectangle are right angles.

questions.prompt: Which shapes always have 4 right angles? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Squares and rectangles always have 4 right angles. A kite usually has none, and a triangle has only 3 angles.

questions.prompt: How many right angles does a right-angled triangle have?
questions.explanation: A right-angled triangle has exactly 1 right angle. Its other 2 angles are smaller.

questions.prompt: Which of these angles is greater than a right angle?
questions.explanation: The corner of paper is a right angle. At 1:00 the hands are close together. At 5:00 they are further apart than at 3:00, so the angle is greater than a right angle.
options: the corner of a sheet of paper
the angle between the clock hands at 1:00
the angle between the clock hands at 5:00

questions.prompt: Aisha says an angle is bigger if its lines are drawn longer. Is she right?
questions.explanation: Making the lines longer does not change how far apart they open. The amount of turn stays the same.
questions.misconception: Judges the size of an angle by the length of its lines.
options: Yes, longer lines make a bigger angle
No, the size of an angle is the amount of turn, not the length of the lines
No, longer lines make a smaller angle

questions.prompt: True or false?
questions.explanation: 2 right angles make a half turn, which is a straight line. If a triangle had 2 right angles, its 2 sides would never meet.

statements.s: 2 right angles together make a straight line.
A triangle can have 2 right angles.
An angle smaller than a right angle is less than a quarter turn.

questions.prompt: Mia turns clockwise through 3 right angles, then 2 more right angles. How many right angles past a complete turn has she gone?
questions.explanation: 3 + 2 = 5 right angles. A complete turn is 4 right angles. 5 − 4 = 1.

units.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
units.summary: Horizontal lines go straight across and vertical lines go straight up and down. Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet, while perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.

questions.prompt: A line that goes straight across, like the horizon, is...
questions.explanation: Horizontal lines go straight across, like the horizon.

questions.prompt: The edge of a door that goes straight up and down is...
questions.explanation: Vertical lines go straight up and down.

questions.prompt: Lines that meet at a right angle are...
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines meet or cross at a right angle.

questions.prompt: How many pairs of parallel sides does a square have?
questions.explanation: The top and bottom are parallel. The 2 sides are parallel too. That is 2 pairs.

questions.prompt: Which of these capital letters have a pair of parallel lines? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: H and N each have 2 vertical lines. E has 3 horizontal lines. L and V have no lines that stay the same distance apart.

questions.prompt: Which of these capital letters have a pair of perpendicular lines? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: T, L and F all have a horizontal line meeting a vertical line at a right angle. V meets at a smaller angle and O has no straight lines.

questions.prompt: The 2 rails of a straight railway track are...
questions.explanation: The rails stay the same distance apart and never meet, so they are parallel.

questions.prompt: Kian says 2 lines are parallel because they are both 5 cm long. Is he right?
questions.explanation: Parallel is about direction, not length. 2 lines are parallel if they stay the same distance apart and never meet.
questions.misconception: Thinks parallel means the same length.
options: Yes, lines of the same length are parallel
No, parallel lines stay the same distance apart; their length does not matter
No, parallel lines must be different lengths

questions.prompt: True or false?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines never meet, however long they are. All 3 sides of a triangle meet each other, so none are parallel.

statements.s: A rectangle has 2 pairs of parallel sides.
A horizontal line and a vertical line that meet are perpendicular.
Parallel lines meet if you make them long enough.
A triangle has a pair of parallel sides.

questions.prompt: How many pairs of perpendicular sides does a rectangle have?
questions.explanation: At each corner 2 sides meet at a right angle. A rectangle has 4 corners, so there are 4 pairs of perpendicular sides.

units.title: Pictograms
units.summary: Always read the key first: one symbol might stand for 2, 5 or 10 things. Half a symbol stands for half of that amount.

questions.prompt:
The pictogram shows the favourite pets of some children.
Key: ● = 4 children, ◐ = 2 children
Cat: ● ● ● ●
Dog: ● ● ● ◐
Fish: ● ◐
Rabbit: ● ●
How many children chose cat?
questions.explanation: Cat has 4 whole circles. Each circle is 4 children. 4 × 4 = 16.

questions.prompt:
The pictogram shows the favourite pets of some children.
Key: ● = 4 children, ◐ = 2 children
Cat: ● ● ● ●
Dog: ● ● ● ◐
Fish: ● ◐
Rabbit: ● ●
How many children chose fish?
questions.explanation: Fish has 1 whole circle (4) and 1 half circle (2). 4 + 2 = 6.

questions.prompt:
The pictogram shows the favourite pets of some children.
Key: ● = 4 children, ◐ = 2 children
Cat: ● ● ● ●
Dog: ● ● ● ◐
Fish: ● ◐
Rabbit: ● ●
How many more children chose dog than rabbit?
questions.explanation: Dog: 3 circles and a half = 12 + 2 = 14. Rabbit: 2 circles = 8. 14 − 8 = 6.

questions.prompt:
The pictogram shows the favourite pets of some children.
Key: ● = 4 children, ◐ = 2 children
Cat: ● ● ● ●
Dog: ● ● ● ◐
Fish: ● ◐
Rabbit: ● ●
How many children are shown in the pictogram altogether?
questions.explanation: Cat 16, dog 14, fish 6, rabbit 8. 16 + 14 + 6 + 8 = 44.

questions.prompt: In a pictogram, 1 circle stands for 10 cars. How would you show 35 cars?
questions.explanation: 3 circles show 30 cars. Half a circle shows 5 more. 30 + 5 = 35.

questions.prompt:
In a pictogram, ● stands for 2 books.
Jamie: ● ● ● ● ◐
How many books did Jamie read?
questions.explanation: 4 whole circles: 4 × 2 = 8 books. Half a circle is 1 book. 8 + 1 = 9.

questions.prompt: In a pictogram, 1 symbol stands for 5 children. A row has 6 symbols. How many children does the row show?
questions.explanation: 6 symbols of 5: 6 × 5 = 30.

questions.prompt:
The pictogram shows the favourite pets of some children.
Key: ● = 4 children, ◐ = 2 children
Cat: ● ● ● ●
Dog: ● ● ● ◐
Fish: ● ◐
Rabbit: ● ●
Rafi says 4 children chose cat because there are 4 circles.
Really, ___ children chose cat.
questions.explanation: The key says each circle is 4 children. 4 circles × 4 = 16 children.
questions.misconception: Counts the symbols without using the key.

questions.prompt:
The pictogram shows the favourite pets of some children.
Key: ● = 4 children, ◐ = 2 children
Cat: ● ● ● ●
Dog: ● ● ● ◐
Fish: ● ◐
Rabbit: ● ●
True or false?
questions.explanation: Cat 16 is double rabbit 8. Dog 14 is 2 fewer than cat, not more. Rabbit and fish: 8 + 6 = 14.

statements.s: Twice as many children chose cat as rabbit.
Fish was the least popular pet.
Dog had 2 more children than cat.
Rabbit and fish together have 14 children.

questions.prompt:
The pictogram shows the favourite pets of some children.
Key: ● = 4 children, ◐ = 2 children
Cat: ● ● ● ●
Dog: ● ● ● ◐
Fish: ● ◐
Rabbit: ● ●
How many whole circles would you need to show the dog and fish children together?
questions.explanation: Dog 14 + fish 6 = 20 children. Each circle is 4 children. 20 ÷ 4 = 5 circles.

units.title: Bar charts
units.summary: Check the scale before you read a bar chart: each line might be worth 2, 5 or 10. Read across from the top of each bar to the scale.

questions.prompt: The bar chart shows birds seen in the school garden. How many sparrows were seen?
questions.explanation: The scale goes up in 2s. The sparrow bar reaches 8.

diagram.title: Birds seen in the school garden

questions.prompt: The bar chart shows birds seen in the school garden. Which bird was seen the most?
questions.explanation: The tallest bar is blue tit, at 18.

diagram.title: Birds seen in the school garden

questions.prompt: How many more blue tits than robins were seen?
questions.explanation: Blue tits 18, robins 12. 18 − 12 = 6.

questions.prompt: The scale on a bar chart goes up in 10s. A bar stops exactly halfway between 30 and 40. What does the bar show?
questions.explanation: Halfway between 30 and 40 is 35, because half of 10 is 5.

questions.prompt: The bar chart shows library books borrowed. How many fewer books were borrowed on Wednesday than on Tuesday?
questions.explanation: The scale goes up in 5s. Tuesday 40, Wednesday 15. 40 − 15 = 25.

questions.prompt: How many books were borrowed on Monday and Thursday together?
questions.explanation: Monday 25, Thursday 30. 25 + 30 = 55.

questions.prompt:
On the birds chart, Lucy says 3 magpies were seen because the magpie bar reaches the 3rd line.
Really, ___ magpies were seen.
questions.explanation: Each line is worth 2, not 1. 3 lines of 2 make 6.
questions.misconception: Counts the lines as 1 each without reading the scale.

diagram.title: Birds seen in the school garden

questions.prompt: Look at the birds chart. True or false?
questions.explanation: Robins 12 is double magpies 6. Sparrows and magpies: 8 + 6 = 14, but blue tits are 18. 12 − 8 = 4.

diagram.title: Birds seen in the school garden

statements.s: Twice as many robins as magpies were seen.
Sparrows and magpies together equal the blue tits.
4 more robins than sparrows were seen.

questions.prompt: How many more books were borrowed on Tuesday and Wednesday together than on Monday?
questions.explanation: Tuesday 40 + Wednesday 15 = 55. Monday 25. 55 − 25 = 30.

units.title: Tables and two-step questions
units.summary: Find the row and column you need in a table and read where they meet. For a two-step question, find the totals first, then compare them.

questions.prompt:
The table shows how many lengths 3 children swam.
Name | Week 1 | Week 2
Ada | 12 | 15
Ben | 9 | 14
Cara | 16 | 11
How many lengths did Ben swim in week 2?
questions.explanation: Find Ben's row and the Week 2 column. They meet at 14.

questions.prompt:
The table shows how many lengths 3 children swam.
Name | Week 1 | Week 2
Ada | 12 | 15
Ben | 9 | 14
Cara | 16 | 11
Who swam the most lengths in week 1?
questions.explanation: Week 1 column: Ada 12, Ben 9, Cara 16. 16 is the most.

questions.prompt:
The table shows how many lengths 3 children swam.
Name | Week 1 | Week 2
Ada | 12 | 15
Ben | 9 | 14
Cara | 16 | 11
How many lengths did Ada swim altogether?
A tally chart shows 2 groups of 5 and 3 more single marks. What number does it show?
questions.explanation: Each group is 5. 5 + 5 + 3 = 13.

questions.prompt:
The table shows how many lengths 3 children swam.
Name | Week 1 | Week 2
Ada | 12 | 15
Ben | 9 | 14
Cara | 16 | 11
How many more lengths did Cara swim than Ben in week 1?

The table shows how many lengths 3 children swam.
Name | Week 1 | Week 2
Ada | 12 | 15
Ben | 9 | 14
Cara | 16 | 11
How many lengths did the 3 children swim altogether in week 2?

The table shows how many lengths 3 children swam.
Name | Week 1 | Week 2
Ada | 12 | 15
Ben | 9 | 14
Cara | 16 | 11
Which 2 children swam the same number of lengths altogether?
questions.explanation: Totals: Ada 12 + 15 = 27, Ben 9 + 14 = 23, Cara 16 + 11 = 27. Ada and Cara both swam 27.

questions.prompt:
The table shows how many lengths 3 children swam.
Name | Week 1 | Week 2
Ada | 12 | 15
Ben | 9 | 14
Cara | 16 | 11
Cara says she swam more lengths in week 2 than in week 1.
She is wrong. Cara swam ___ fewer lengths in week 2.
questions.explanation: Cara swam 16 in week 1 and 11 in week 2. 16 − 11 = 5 fewer.
questions.misconception: Reads the columns the wrong way round.

questions.prompt:
The table shows how many lengths 3 children swam.
Name | Week 1 | Week 2
Ada | 12 | 15
Ben | 9 | 14
Cara | 16 | 11
True or false?
questions.explanation: Week 1: 12 + 9 + 16 = 37. Week 2: 40. Ada swam the most in week 2, with 15.

statements.s: The children swam more lengths in week 2 than in week 1.
Ada swam 3 more lengths in week 2 than in week 1.
Cara swam the most lengths in week 2.

questions.prompt:
The table shows how many lengths 3 children swam.
Name | Week 1 | Week 2
Ada | 12 | 15
Ben | 9 | 14
Cara | 16 | 11
In week 3, Ada swam 5 more lengths than she did in week 2. Ben swam half as many lengths as Ada did in week 3. How many lengths did Ben swim in week 3?
questions.explanation: Ada week 3: 15 + 5 = 20. Half of 20 is 10.
